previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes, morbid obesity, atrial fibrillation, and prior strokes was admitted for evaluation of rapidly spreading blisters and redness on the left foot. Dermatology diagnosed bullous diabeticorum, and the patient received IV antibiotics as a precaution. A minor procedure was performed to drain a large blister. Despite medical advice to stay overnight, the patient left against medical advice the evening of admission. He was discharged on his home medications with instructions to keep the wound dressing clean and dry and to follow up promptly with outpatient care. No oral antibiotics were prescribed at discharge.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ male with PMHx poorly-controlled diabetes, 
systolic CHF, and chronic foot ulcerations followed by podiatry 
presenting with chills and found to have gas gangrene of his 
first right metatarsal, post-operative course complicated by 
persistent hypotension requiring MICU admission. He was fluid 
resuscitated with improvement ___ BP and transferred to the 
medical floor

ACUTE ISSUES:

# Hypotension
Post-operatively developed hypotension with SBP ___ the ___. 
___ be related to sedation (propofol and midazolam during the 
case) or sepsis (has a leukocytosis) from likely infected right 
hallux. No clear evidence of pneumonia or UTI. No concern for 
biliary sepsis. He was fluid resuscitated with small boluses 
given known systolic heart failure with improvement ___ BP and 
normalization of lactate. He was treated with antibiotics as 
below for infected hallux. Patients pressures improved and were 
stable on the floor.

# Sepsis from Gas Gangrene
Presented with gas gangrene of his first right hallux and sepsis 
as evidenced by leukocytosis, tachycardia. He underwent open 
partial amputation with podiatry. He was started on vancomycin 
and zosyn. He underwent a second debridement and wound vacuum 
placement. Patient was seen by the infectious disease team who 
suggested that the patinet be continued on zosyn with 
discontinuation of vancomycin. They suggested zosyn be switched 
to ertapenem on discharge. PICC was placed during hospital stay. 
Infectious disease will follow him as an outpatient and 
recommended 6 weeks of IV ertapenem.  

# Hypoxemia
Post-operatively had hypoxemia with a 5L NC requirement. 
Pre-operative CXR with evidence of some pulmonary edema ___ the 
setting of known systolic CHF. Low suspicion for pneumonia, but 
this is a possibility given leukocytosis. Unlikley PE given lack 
of tachcyardia and INR is supratherapeutic. Was notably more 
hypoxic when sleeping; does have known OSA but declines CPAP. 
His oxygen was titrated to room air within 24 hours of 
admission. Patient continued to have hypoxic spells while 
sleeping be declined any supplemental oxygen. He complained of 
orthopnea that was likely secondary to his systolic heart 
failure, immobility and holding of his blood pressure 
medications.  

# Hyperbilirubinemia
Presented with new elevated total bilirubin. Has no RUQ pain, no 
clear evidence of hemolysis. Has prior hepatitis serologies ___ 
___, HCV Ab negative and non-immune to hepatitis B. Cholestasis 
of sepsis was felt to be the predominant etiology. RUQ 
ultrasound showed gallbladder swelling. No evidence of 
cholecystitis. Patients liver enzymes started to down trend.  

# Coagulopathy
Anticoagulated on warfarin for atrial fibrillation. Presented 
with INR elevated to 7.2 on admission peaked at 9, most recently 
2.8 one month ago. Was on a course of levofloxacin at the end of 
___ for presumably foot infection. He did have bleeding of his 
foot s/p amputation and was given low-dose IV vitamin K to 
reverse his INR.  Warafarin was held. Patient was titrated back 
on his warfarin for a goal INR of ___ and was bridged on 
enoxaparin during his stay. His INR was 2.4 on discharge.

# Diabetes
Uncontrolled, last A1C 8.1%. Was told to restart on his prior 
insulin by his PCP. He states that he takes 45U Humilin ___ the 
morning. However, he has not always been compliant with this. 
Started on humalog sliding scale. He was started on 30U of 
Huilin with breakfast and dinner ___ addition to a sliding scale. 
His sugars were stable. 

# Chronic systolic heart failure
EF of 40-45%, on torsemide at home 40-60mg daily adjusted for 
leg edema. Does have some mild pulmonary edema but no clear 
decompensation. Torsemide, spironolactone, and rampiril were 
initially held given hypotension. Patient started to complain of 
orthopnea and worsening shortness of breath similar to what he 
experiences at home when he is fluid overloaded. He was 
restarted on his torsemide at 40mg PO. He was diuresed over 2L 
and his symptoms started to improve. He needs continued diuresis 
as he is fluid overloaded. His ramparil and spironolactone will 
need to be restarted as an outpatient. 

#Wrist swelling ___ to IV infiltration- patient had wrist 
swelling and pain during his stay thought to be due to IV 
infiltration. Patient was advised to keep his wrist elevated and 
was not always compliant. His swelling did continue to improve. 

#Acute Kideny Injury- patient had bump ___ cr from 1.1 to 1.3 ___ 
setting of diuresis. Could be caused by toresemide, or possible 
due to pre-renal etiology secondary to CHF. Cr was stable. 
Patient was continued to be diuresed. 

TRANSLATIONAL ISSUES:
#Patient also will need to have his INR checked and his warfarin 
dose titrated. 
#Diuresis with torsemide, when his creatinine stablizes and his 
blood pressures are stable he can be restarted on ramirpil and 
sprionolactone. 
#6 weeks of IV ertapenem 1g q24h- follow up with Infectious 
disease doctors for outpatient ___ therapy 
#WEEKLY: CBC with differential, BUN, Cr, AST, ALT, TB, ALK PHOS
*PLEASE OBTAIN WEEKLY ESR/CRP for patients with bone/joint
infections and endocarditis or endovascular infections
